question.text: Lotus Growth AIF is a Category II fund with a target corpus of INR 800 crore. The sponsor, Mr. Ramesh Iyer's family office, is finalising skin-in-the-game. As per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012, what is the minimum continuing interest the sponsor must maintain?

answer.text: INR 20 crore (2.5% of corpus, since it is higher than INR 5 crore cap)
INR 40 crore (5% of corpus, Category III rule applied)
INR 5 crore (2.5% of corpus OR INR 5 crore, whichever is LOWER)
INR 8 crore (1% of corpus, minimum manager contribution)

explanation.text: The Logic: For Category I and II AIFs, sponsor/manager continuing interest is the LOWER of 2.5% of corpus OR INR 5 crore. 2.5% of INR 800 crore = INR 20 crore; the lower figure is INR 5 crore, which becomes the floor commitment. This must be a cash investment, not a management-fee waiver or stock transfer. The Trap: Option A mis-reads 'whichever is lower' as 'whichever is higher'. Option B applies the Cat III formula (5%/INR 10 cr) to a Cat II fund. Option D invents a 1% figure that does not exist in the regulations. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) tests this same threshold from the sales angle. XIX-B uses the Cat III threshold (5%/INR 10 cr). Managers preparing for XIX-C should also know Angel Fund commitment is 0.5% or INR 50,000 whichever is HIGHER. Manager's Pro-Tip: When negotiating LP documentation, sponsors often voluntarily commit more than the regulatory floor (5-10% is common for first-time funds) to signal conviction. Disclose this delta in the PPM — LPs read 'regulatory minimum only' as weak alignment.
